name: Warm-season lawn (Bermuda, Zoysia, St. Augustine, Centipede): 5-step program
title: 🌱 Lawn Care Tracker: Warm-Season Lawn
intro: **Program:** a brand-neutral plan for **Bermuda, Zoysia, St. Augustine, Centipede and Bahia** (the South, Southwest and transition zone). Steps note species differences.
**Dates** come from your location's frost dates; 📡 weather triggers then fine-tune each step for your yard.
sources: University extension warm-season lawn calendars (Texas A&M AgriLife, UF/IFAS, Clemson HGIC, NC State TurfFiles)

steps.name: Prep Tasks
steps.heading: 🧹 Prep Tasks
steps.note: Sharpen blades, service the mower, calibrate the spreader, consider a soil test.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Equipment:** sharpen mower blades, change the oil, calibrate the spreader.
- **Soil test (recommended):** your state's extension service reports pH and nutrients. Centipede and St. Augustine prefer slightly acidic soil.
- **Know your grass:** Bermuda and Zoysia (sun, fine texture) · St. Augustine (wide blades, shade-tolerant) · Centipede (low-input, light green) · Bahia. Steps below note species differences.

steps.name: Step 1: Spring Pre-Emergent (no fertilizer yet)
steps.heading: 🛡️ Step 1: Spring Pre-Emergent (no fertilizer yet)
steps.note: Crabgrass/goosegrass preventer before soil holds 55°F. Don't fertilize yet; warm-season grass is still dormant. Water in.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a **pre-emergent only** (prodiamine or dithiopyr), **not** a weed & feed. Fertilizer now feeds weeds, not the dormant grass.
- **Timing cue:** 📡 soil reaching a 7-day average of 50°F, before crabgrass sprouts at ~55°F.
- Water in with ½" within 2–3 days.
- Planning to plug or sod bare spots this year? Keep the preventer off those areas.
steps.buy_item: pre-emergent herbicide (prodiamine or dithiopyr, no fertilizer)

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" hit a 7-day average of {val} on {date}. Crabgrass sprouts once soil holds ~55°F, so apply now.

steps.name: Green-Up: Scalp & Start Mowing
steps.heading: ✂️ Green-Up: Scalp & Start Mowing
steps.note: Bermuda/Zoysia: scalp low and bag clippings as green-up starts. St. Augustine/Centipede: just mow normally. Turn irrigation on.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Bermuda & Zoysia:** scalp (mow 1–1.5" lower than normal, bag the clippings) once the grass starts greening. It removes dead thatch and speeds green-up. Dethatch only if thatch is over ½".
- **St. Augustine & Centipede:** don't scalp; just remove debris and mow at normal height.
- **Irrigation:** turn on, check heads, set to manual. Water only when the lawn shows stress.

trigger.basis: Soil reached a 5-day average of {val} on {date}. Green-up is starting.

steps.name: Step 2: First Feeding (after full green-up)
steps.heading: 🌱 Step 2: First Feeding (after full green-up)
steps.note: Feed once the lawn is fully green and soil holds 65°F. Bermuda/Zoysia: full rate. St. Augustine: moderate. Centipede: light, low-phosphorus.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Wait for **full green-up**: soil holding 65°F and you've mowed 2–3 times. 📡 The calendar times it from soil temperature.
- **Bermuda / Zoysia:** lawn fertilizer at the bag rate (about 1 lb N/1,000 sq ft).
- **St. Augustine:** ½–1 lb N; slow-release with iron.
- **Centipede:** at most ½ lb N with little or no phosphorus; it declines when over-fed.
- Water in.

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" averaging {val} (since {since}). The grass is out of dormancy and can use the food.

steps.name: Spring Weed Control
steps.heading: 🌼 Spring Weed Control
steps.note: Spot-spray broadleaf weeds on a mild, dry day. St. Augustine & Centipede: use atrazine-type products; many 2,4-D mixes injure them.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Spot-treat **broadleaf weeds** (clover, dandelion, henbit) with a product **labeled for your grass**.
- **St. Augustine & Centipede** are sensitive to 2,4-D blends: use atrazine or a product labeled for them.
- 📡 The calendar picks a ⭐ best day: 65–85°F and no rain for 24 hrs. Don't spray during green-up stress or above 90°F.
steps.buy_item: post-emergent weed killer labeled for your grass type

best.note: {day}: high {hi}, no rain. Good spraying day.

trigger.basis: Highs 70°F+ for 3 days (since {since}). Weeds are actively growing and take up the spray.

steps.name: Grub Preventer
steps.heading: 🐛 Grub Preventer
steps.note: Chlorantraniliprole (e.g. GrubEx) before beetles lay eggs; water in ½".
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a preventive grub control (**chlorantraniliprole** is the lowest-toxicity option and lasts the season). Water in ½".
- **Skip** if you've never had grub damage; do a quick check in late summer instead.

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" averaging {val}. Grub preventer goes down before beetles lay eggs.

steps.name: Mosquito Season Start
steps.heading: 🦟 Mosquito Season Start
steps.note: Dump standing water weekly; Bti dunks for water you can't dump; optional barrier spray on shrubs every 3–4 weeks.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Dump standing water weekly** (buckets, saucers, gutters, toys).
- **Bti dunks** in bird baths, rain barrels and ponds; replace monthly.
- **Optional barrier spray** on shrubs and shady foliage, not flowers. The calendar repeats it every 25 days through early fall.

trigger.basis: Nights have stayed above 55°F for 5 days (since {since}). Mosquito season is starting.

steps.name: Step 3: Summer Feeding
steps.heading: ☀️ Step 3: Summer Feeding
steps.note: About 6 weeks after Step 2. Bermuda/Zoysia: full rate. St. Augustine: half rate, slow-release. Centipede: skip.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Bermuda:** full rate; it's a heavy feeder in summer. **Zoysia:** moderate.
- **St. Augustine:** half rate, slow-release; heavy summer nitrogen invites chinch bugs and gray leaf spot.
- **Centipede:** skip it.
- Water in. Avoid applying during drought or 95°F+ heat.

trigger.basis: About 6 weeks after your first feeding ({anchor}).

steps.name: Summer Mode: Mowing & Watering
steps.heading: ☀️ Summer Mode: Mowing & Watering
steps.note: Water 1–1.5"/week in 1–2 deep early-morning sessions. Mow at your species' summer height; never remove more than 1/3.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Mowing heights:** Bermuda 1–2" · Zoysia 1.5–2.5" · St. Augustine 3–4" · Centipede 1.5–2". Never remove more than 1/3 at a time.
- **Watering:** 1–1.5"/week (rain + irrigation) in 1–2 deep sessions, **4–9 AM**. Water when blades fold or footprints stay visible.
- **Watch for:** chinch bugs in hot, sunny St. Augustine (yellow patches that spread); armyworms in Bermuda after storms.

trigger.basis: Highs 90°F+ for 3 days (since {since}). Switch to summer watering and mowing.

steps.name: Optional: Second Summer Feeding (Bermuda)
steps.heading: 🍃 Optional: Second Summer Feeding (Bermuda)
steps.note: OPTIONAL, mainly for Bermuda you want dense and dark. Skip for St. Augustine and Centipede, or in drought.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- For **Bermuda** (and Zoysia if thin): another slow-release feeding about 6 weeks after Step 3.
- **Skip** for St. Augustine and Centipede, and during drought or heat waves.

trigger.basis: About 6 weeks after your summer feeding ({anchor}). Bermuda only; skip in drought.

steps.name: Repair Bare Spots (sod, plugs or seed)
steps.heading: 🌾 Repair Bare Spots (sod, plugs or seed)
steps.note: Warm-season grass spreads best in early summer: sod or plug Zoysia/St. Augustine/Centipede; seed Bermuda once soil holds 65°F+.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Best window:** early summer, when soil holds 65°F+ and the grass is actively spreading. 📡 Timed from soil temperature.
- **Bermuda:** seed at the bag rate (hulled seed), rake in lightly, keep moist.
- **Zoysia, St. Augustine, Centipede:** use **sod or plugs** (seed is slow or unavailable).
- **Water:** keep new sod/seed moist (light watering 2–3×/day) for 2–3 weeks, then taper. Seedling watering alerts run 4 weeks after you mark this done.
- No pre-emergent on repaired spots this season.
steps.buy_item: sod, plugs or Bermuda seed + starter fertilizer

trigger.basis: Soil holding {val} (since {since}). Warm-season grass roots and spreads fastest now.

steps.name: Step 4: Fall Pre-Emergent (winter weeds)
steps.heading: 🛡️ Step 4: Fall Pre-Emergent (winter weeds)
steps.note: Prevents winter weeds (Poa annua, henbit, chickweed). Apply as soil cools toward 70°F. Skip where you'll overseed ryegrass.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a **pre-emergent** (prodiamine or dithiopyr) as soil cools toward 70°F. This is the step that keeps **Poa annua, henbit and chickweed** out of a dormant lawn.
- Water in ½".
- **Skip** areas you'll overseed with winter ryegrass (O2).

trigger.basis: Soil cooled to a 5-day average of {val} on {date}. Winter weeds start sprouting soon.

steps.name: Step 5: Last Feeding / Potassium (no late nitrogen)
steps.heading: 🍂 Step 5: Last Feeding / Potassium (no late nitrogen)
steps.note: Stop nitrogen about 6 weeks before your first frost. Optional potassium (0-0-50 or similar) for winter hardiness.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Timing:** about 6 weeks before your typical first frost (a fixed date for your area, not weather-timed).
- **No nitrogen after this point.** Late nitrogen on warm-season grass invites winter kill and spring disease (large patch).
- **Optional:** potassium (e.g. 0-0-50 or a "fall" warm-season blend) builds cold and disease tolerance, especially for Bermuda and St. Augustine.
- There's **no winterizer** for warm-season grass; the cool-season "winterizer" advice doesn't apply.

steps.name: Large Patch Prevention (optional fungicide)
steps.heading: 🍄 Large Patch Prevention (optional fungicide)
steps.note: If you've had large patch (orange-ringed circles in spring/fall), apply a preventive fungicide as soil cools to 70°F. Avoid late-day watering.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Large patch** shows up as orange/brown rings in Zoysia, St. Augustine and Centipede when soil is 60–70°F and wet.
- If you've had it before: preventive fungicide (azoxystrobin, propiconazole) as soil cools through 70°F; repeat per label.
- Water early morning only, and fix drainage. Don't fertilize heavily in fall.
steps.buy_item: lawn fungicide (if you've had large patch)

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" cooling through {val}. That's large-patch season.

steps.name: Optional: Overseed Winter Ryegrass (Bermuda)
steps.heading: 🌱 Optional: Overseed Winter Ryegrass (Bermuda)
steps.note: OPTIONAL for green winter Bermuda: perennial ryegrass at 8–10 lb/1,000 sq ft as nights cool. Skip the fall pre-emergent on these areas.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- For a green lawn all winter on **Bermuda**: scalp low, then seed **perennial ryegrass** at 8–10 lb/1,000 sq ft. Keep moist until it's up.
- Don't overseed Zoysia, St. Augustine or Centipede; it competes with them in spring.
- No fall pre-emergent (Step 4) where you overseed.

trigger.basis: Soil cooling to {val}. Ryegrass establishes now while Bermuda slows down.

steps.name: Fall Watering Shift
steps.heading: 💧 Fall Watering Shift
steps.note: Cut back to about ½–1"/week, only when needed. Raise the mower a notch for the last few cuts.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Reduce watering to **½–1"/week** including rain, only when needed; dormant grass needs little.
- Raise the mower slightly for the last few cuts going into dormancy.

trigger.basis: Cooler weather since {date}. Cut back watering.

steps.name: Leaf Management
steps.heading: 🍁 Leaf Management
steps.note: Mulch-mow light leaf cover; rake heavy mats so they don't smother dormant grass.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Mulch-mow** light leaf cover. **Rake** heavy layers; matted leaves smother dormant grass and invite disease.

steps.name: Dormancy & Close-Out
steps.heading: 🔒 Dormancy & Close-Out
steps.note: Lawn goes dormant (tan) after frost: normal. Winterize irrigation where pipes can freeze; keep traffic off frosty grass.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Tan after frost is normal dormancy** for warm-season grass. Don't fertilize or over-water it.
- **Irrigation:** where hard freezes happen, drain or blow out lines before the first one.
- **Winter watering:** water dormant grass every 3–4 weeks in dry, windy winters, on a mild day.
- **Next season:** a 🔄 reminder before spring resets the tracker in one tap.

trigger.basis: First hard freeze (low {val}) forecast for {trig}. Winterize irrigation before then.
